title_en: Russia's own figures show almost 500,000 deaths in war in Ukraine
title_zh: 俄罗斯自己的数据显示近50万人在乌克兰战争中死亡
summary: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.
summary_zh: 泄露的数据揭示了对乌克兰的全面入侵如何从根本上改变了俄罗斯的死亡率模式。
body_en: By Olga Ivshina , BBC Russian and Yaroslava Kiryukhina , BBC Russian
At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.

The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.
BBC Russian has had access to more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow.
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.

Together with independent Russian outlet Mediazona, BBC Russian has compared the Rosstat data with its own list of confirmed military deaths, pulled from open sources since the start of the invasion, and it has found matches for 90% of the records.

The records show that 65% of 18 to 24 year-olds in Russia who lost their lives in 2025 died in the war. For those aged 25-34 the number was 59%. Only among 45 to 54 year-olds does cardiovascular disease claim more Russian lives than the conflict.
The data also reveal the extent of losses in specific areas of Ukraine. Some 20,000 Russian soldiers died fighting for control of 10 Ukrainian villages whose combined pre-war population was 12,000.
During the fight for one small village called Andriivka, south of the town of Bakhmut in Donetsk region, 1,122 Russians lost their lives. Before the war 74 people lived there.

Russia does not give public figures for losses sustained since the war began in February 2022. And two years ago Rosstat stopped publishing data of deaths from external causes, which was used to gauge the extent of military losses.

For example, only 70% of deaths we have established of soldiers from the occupied regions of Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine who fought in the Russian army were accounted for in the Rosstat files.
The Rosstat dataset contains no names but does include ages, places of residence, places of death and also circumstances of death.
We have filtered the records first by location, leaving only Ukraine as well as Russian border regions that saw incursions by the Ukrainian army.
Next, we identified 425,174 entries explicitly indicating a military-related cause of death, such as explosions or shrapnel during combat operations.

As this count could include civilians, we filtered out women as well as men outside the 18-65 age group. And if someone lived and died in the four Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, we excluded them as a possible civilian – unless he had a record of military service attached to his entry.

Another 14,093 entries were identified by looking at employment, and 51,067 were recorded in the database as deceased on the basis of a court ruling. This often happens when a soldier goes missing in a combat zone for more than six months and their body has not been recovered.
Again, we filtered out civilians by only counting deaths in the war zones in Ukraine and Russia.

BBC Russian's own detailed records of Russian losses has reached 290,012, verified together with Mediazona from official reports, social media, new memorials and graves. The actual death toll is likely to be higher, as not all deaths are reported publicly.
Overall, the Rosstat dataset confirms the trends that we have observed with our own count.

According to BBC Russian's analysis of the leaked files, in the first year of the war the average age of those killed was 34. By 2025, as prisoners and contract soldiers entered the ranks, it had risen to 40 (38 according to our own list).
body_zh: 作者：Olga Ivshina，BBC 俄语 和 Yaroslava Kiryukhina，BBC 俄语
BBC 分析的俄罗斯政府统计数据显示，自 2022 年乌克兰战争爆发以来，至少有 490,334 名俄罗斯士兵死亡。
俄罗斯统计局泄露的数据揭示了对乌克兰的全面入侵如何从根本上改变了俄罗斯的死亡率模式，并显示了弗拉基米尔·普京原以为这场战争只会持续几天，但现在已经持续了近五年，人类生命付出了高昂的代价。
在白俄罗斯组织 Cyber​​ Partisans BY 和乌克兰 Silent Crow 黑客攻击后，BBC 俄语频道从 2021 年到 2026 年 9 月获得了超过 1100 万条死亡记录。
俄罗斯统计机构承认遭受了网络攻击，但否认任何受保护的信息被泄露。
BBC Russian 与俄罗斯独立媒体 Mediazona 合作，将 Rosstat 的数据与自入侵开始以来从公开来源获取的已确认军人死亡名单进行了比较，发现 90% 的记录都匹配。
记录显示，2025年丧生的俄罗斯18至24岁青少年中有65%死于战争。对于25-34岁的人来说，这一比例为59%。只有 45 至 54 岁的俄罗斯人死于心血管疾病的人数比冲突还多。
数据还揭示了乌克兰特定地区的损失程度。大约 20,000 名俄罗斯士兵在争夺 10 个乌克兰村庄的控制权的战斗中牺牲，这些村庄战前的总人口为 12,000 人。
在顿涅茨克地区巴赫穆特镇以南一个名叫安德里夫卡的小村庄的战斗中，1,122 名俄罗斯人丧生。战前有 74 人住在那里。
俄罗斯没有公布自 2022 年 2 月战争开始以来遭受的损失的公开数据。两年前，俄罗斯统计局停止发布外因死亡数据，该数据用于衡量军事损失的程度。
例如，在我们确定的来自乌克兰东部顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克被占领地区的、在俄罗斯军队中作战的士兵中，只有 70% 的死亡记录在俄罗斯统计局的档案中。
Rosstat 数据集不包含姓名，但包含年龄、居住地、死亡地点以及死亡情况。
我们首先按地点过滤记录，只留下乌克兰和俄罗斯边境地区遭受过乌克兰军队的入侵。
接下来，我们确定了 425,174 个条目，明确表明与军事相关的死亡原因，例如战斗行动期间的爆炸或弹片。
由于此计数可能包括平民，因此我们过滤掉了 18-65 岁年龄组之外的女性和男性。如果有人在俄罗斯占领的乌克兰四个地区生活和死亡，我们会将他们排除在可能的平民之外——除非他入境时附有服兵役记录。
通过查看就业情况，还确定了另外 14,093 名条目，根据法院裁决，数据库中记录了 51,067 名死亡者。当一名士兵在战区失踪六个月以上且尸体尚未找到时，通常会发生这种情况。
我们再次通过仅计算乌克兰和俄罗斯战区的死亡人数来过滤掉平民。
BBC Russian 自己的俄罗斯损失详细记录已达 290,012 条，与 Mediazona 一起通过官方报道、社交媒体、新纪念碑和坟墓进行核实。实际死亡人数可能更高，因为并非所有死亡都被公开报道。
总体而言，Rosstat 数据集证实了我们通过自己的统计观察到的趋势。
根据BBC俄语对泄露文件的分析，战争第一年，阵亡者的平均年龄为34岁。到2025年，随着战俘和合同兵入伍，阵亡者的平均年龄已上升至40岁（根据我们自己的名单，阵亡者的平均年龄为38岁）。

title_en: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
title_zh: 以色列空袭杀死加沙哈马斯内部安全负责人
summary: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.
summary_zh: 已经任职两个月的纳伊姆·阿布·纳赫勒是据报道在周二以色列袭击中丧生的七名巴勒斯坦人之一。
body_en: At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.

Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.
The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.

Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.

Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.
The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.
Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.
Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.

The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".
It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".

Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".

Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.

The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.
On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.
Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it said.

Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.
body_zh: 卫生官员和急救人员表示，至少七名巴勒斯坦人在以色列对加沙地带的空袭中丧生，其中包括一名哈马斯高级安全官员。
加沙哈马斯内政部表示，哈马斯内部安全部门负责人纳伊姆·阿布·纳赫尔在加沙城西部成为袭击目标。这位 50 岁的人自 9 月份以来才担任这一职务，当时他的前任在以色列特种部队的一次突袭中被抓获。
以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡和国防部长以色列·卡茨宣布阿布·纳赫勒被以色列军方“消灭”。
另外六人在加沙其他地方早些时候的两次空袭中丧生。
据卫生官员和急救人员称，加沙城以南的加沙瓦迪地区有三人死亡，其中包括一名十几岁的男孩。他们补充说，另外三人在汗尤尼斯以西的马瓦西地区的一个警察局被杀。
隶属内政部的加沙警察部队表示，在第二次袭击中丧生的有两名警官。它还指责以色列“正在进行一场针对警察机构的行动，旨在在该领土上制造混乱”。
以色列军方表示，它袭击了这两个地区的“军事人员”。
目击者称，一架以色列无人机袭击了纳伊姆·阿布·纳赫勒，当时他正走在加沙城流离失所者帐篷营地附近的一条小街上。
据报道，另有几人在罢工中受重伤。
以色列军方表示，阿布·纳赫勒对哈马斯内部安全部门“拥有广泛的机构知识”，该部门负责执行纪律、保护基础设施和铲除线人，他的死亡“对该机构的管理能力构成了打击”。
它还声称，他在战争期间对以色列军队和平民进行了高级袭击，并杀死了他“以消除他构成的威胁”。
加沙内政部表示，阿布·纳赫勒被杀之前，其称国内安全部门“在打击与占领[以色列]勾结并在其军队控制的地区活动的团伙方面取得了重要成就”。
自去年10月以色列和哈马斯在美国斡旋下达成停火协议以来，加沙地带的暴力活动一直在持续。以色列几乎每天都会在哈马斯控制的地区发动袭击，该地区居住着 210 万人，其中大多数人流离失所。
据哈马斯管理的加沙卫生部称，过去 13 个月，加沙至少有 1,679 人被杀，联合国认为该数字可靠。
以色列称，同一时期有六名以色列士兵在加沙被杀。
人道主义局势依然严峻，本月早些时候的强降雨导致洪水泛滥，数千个流离失所家庭的住所遭到破坏。
联合国及其合作伙伴呼吁控制加沙过境点的以色列提供更多物资，帮助巴勒斯坦人过冬，包括帐篷、加热器和水泵，以及对抗传染病的疫苗和药物。
周二，卫生部警告说，脑膜炎病例迅速增加，10 月份报告了 272 例，约为平时月平均水平的八倍。
报告称，今年迄今为止已有 15 人因感染死亡，其中 8 月至 10 月期间报告了 5 人死亡。
以色列军事机构 Cogat 周一表示，它正在“努力提供专门的人道主义应对措施”，并在与联合国机构的会议上提交了新批准的一揽子水泵、发电机、水罐车和医疗设备。

title_en: UK warns companies of potential Russian sabotage threat
title_zh: 英国警告企业注意俄罗斯潜在的破坏威胁
summary: Britain's Defence Ministry and security service warn of the threat in unusual public announcement.
summary_zh: 英国国防部和安全部门以不同寻常的公开声明警告这一威胁。
body_en: UK warns companies of potential Russian sabotage threat | Espionage News | Al Jazeera
Share UK warns companies of potential Russian sabotage threat on social media
Britain’s Defence Ministry and the country’s security service, known as MI5, are warning companies that support Ukraine’s military that they may face attempted sabotage from Russia.

“If your organisation supports military procurement or supplies equipment to Ukraine’s armed forces, it could be a target,” the Ministry of Defence and the National Protective Security Authority said in an unusual public announcement on Tuesday.

“This activity is typically characterised by the use of proxy actors employing low-sophistication sabotage methodologies, such as arson,” the warning said, urging companies to take action against security threats posed by what they described as operatives acting for Russia.
Russia’s embassy in London denied such claims in a statement and said: “Russia has no plans, reasons or intentions to attack the UK.”
It also accused Ukraine of carrying out sabotage to “put the blame on Russia and extort more money from western governments”, something Kyiv has repeatedly denied.
Since the Ukraine war started and Britain became one of Kyiv’s key supporters, London has accused Russia of being behind a number of spying and sabotage plots.

Last year, three British men were convicted for an arson attack on a warehouse storing Starlink satellite equipment bound for Ukraine, which prosecutors said was carried out by Russian military intelligence agents.
In September, a man was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service after alleged contact with Russian military spies.

On Sunday, Estonia said it would close all its border crossing points with Russia following a suspected sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company, while last week the Norwegian security service said it expected Russian intelligence to carry out sabotage attacks in Norway in the coming year.

Britain’s Ministry of Defence said it was holding closed-door security briefings with leaders from the critical national infrastructure and defence sectors over the next two days to advise on security.
“Recent sabotage attempts right across Europe demonstrate the seriousness of the threats we face,” Security Minister Dan Jarvis said.
“It’s truly shameful that actors are seeking to disrupt our way of life and that of our allies, especially targeting organisations doing vital work in support of Ukraine.”

title_en: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
title_zh: 泄露的数据显示，莫斯科支持马里军政府导致 300 多名俄罗斯人死亡
summary: Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour,
summary_zh: 独家：记录显示马里三年内有 349 人死亡，同时也揭示了俄罗斯在非洲其他地区的军事活动
body_en: Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

W hen the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”
Russia’s war dead: the hidden toll of the Ukraine conflict

The Kremlin-controlled forces and their Malian allies were facing a coordinated surprise assault by the al-Qaida-linked JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), whose fighters used suicide car bombs and drones to break through the city’s defences.

Leaked Russian state records suggest the losses were heavy that day. Death certificates of Russian fighters killed in Mali , held by Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, were obtained by the hacker groups Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow and analysed by the Guardian.

The records show that 43 Russians died in Mali on 25 April, including six in Kidal and one in nearby Aguelhok. Others were recorded as dying in the capital, Bamako, and in Gao, where rebels shot down a Russian military helicopter that day.

By the following morning, the Russians had abandoned Kidal, which Russian mercenaries had helped capture in November 2023 and which Moscow had since held up as a showcase of its growing influence in Africa.
In all, the records list 349 Russian deaths in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026, most of which the Guardian was able to link to known battles with rebel groups.
The figures offer a previously unseen glimpse into the human cost of Moscow’s efforts to prop up Mali’s military junta, in what has become Russia’s largest military deployment in Africa.
Two western officials who have travelled to Mali and were shown the data said the death toll was higher than previously estimated.
“That’s over 10% of Russia’s forces killed in action,” said one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.
Leaked data shows more than 1,000 Russian military suicides during Ukraine war
Moscow does not publish its losses in Africa, and its foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

The Wagner private military group, led by the warlord Yevgeny Prigozhin, first arrived in Mali in late 2021, a year after a military coup had toppled President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta. French forces were ordered to leave the country as relations with the junta deteriorated, bringing an end to France’s decade-long counter-terrorism operation and leaving Russia as the regime’s main foreign protector.

Wagner handed over its operations in Mali to the Africa Corps in June 2025, two years after Prigozhin led a failed mutiny on Moscow that discredited the group in the eyes of the Kremlin. By that summer, British intelligence estimated that about 2,000 Africa Corps personnel were deployed in the country.

The Africa Corps, closely overseen by Russian military intelligence, currently provides backing to several African governments in return for payment or lucrative contracts granting access to natural resources.

Despite the Russian presence, Mali’s security situation has continued to deteriorate. In late July 2024, Russian and Malian forces fought Tuareg separatists for several days near Tinzaouaten, on the Algerian border.
Wagner at the time issued a rare statement admitting losses, including the death of a commander, but gave no figure. Estimates from Russian sources ranged from about 20 to more than 80 dead.
body_zh: 独家：记录显示马里三年内有 349 人死亡，同时也揭示了俄罗斯在非洲其他地区的军事活动
W hen the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard.在第一个小时内，这座坐落在马里北部岩石山丘之间的偏远沙漠城市郊区的检查站就被叛乱分子占领，他们向警察局推进，在那里爆发了激烈的战斗。
“一切都同时发生。我们周围爆炸，人们大喊大叫，”一位当时驻扎在马里的前俄罗斯非洲军团成员回忆道，他不愿透露姓名。 “没有人知道敌人从哪里来。”
俄罗斯的战争死难者：乌克兰冲突的隐性伤亡
克里姆林宫控制的部队及其马里盟友正面临与基地组织有联系的 JNIM 和图阿雷格人领导的阿扎瓦德解放阵线 (FLA) 的协调突然袭击，该阵线的战士使用自杀式汽车炸弹和无人机突破了该市的防御。
泄露的俄罗斯国家记录显示，当天损失惨重。黑客组织 Cyber​​ Partisans 和 Silent Crow 获得了俄罗斯国家统计机构 Rosstat 持有的在马里阵亡的俄罗斯战士的死亡证明，并由《卫报》进行了分析。
记录显示，4 月 25 日有 43 名俄罗斯人在马里死亡，其中 6 人死于基达尔，1 人死于附近的阿盖洛克。据记录，首都巴马科和加奥的其他人死亡，叛军当天击落了一架俄罗斯军用直升机。
到第二天早上，俄罗斯人已经放弃了基达尔，俄罗斯雇佣军于 2023 年 11 月帮助占领了基达尔，莫斯科此后一直将基达尔作为其在非洲日益增长的影响力的展示。
总而言之，记录列出了 2023 年 9 月至 2026 年 9 月期间，俄罗斯人在马里死亡 349 人，《卫报》能够将其中大部分与已知的与叛乱组织的战斗联系起来。
这些数字让人们得以一睹莫斯科为支持马里军政府而付出的人力代价，这已成为俄罗斯在非洲最大规模的军事部署。
两名前往马里并看到数据的西方官员表示，死亡人数高于之前的估计。
一位不愿透露姓名的官员表示，“超过 10% 的俄罗斯军队在行动中阵亡”，因为他们无权公开发表评论。
泄露数据显示乌克兰战争期间已有1000多名俄罗斯军人自杀
莫斯科没有公布其在非洲的损失，其外交部也没有回应置评请求。
由军阀叶夫根尼·普里戈任 (Yevgeny Prigozhin) 领导的瓦格纳私人军事团体于 2021 年底首次抵达马里，一年前，一场军事政变推翻了总统易卜拉欣·布巴卡尔·凯塔 (Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta)。随着与军政府关系恶化，法国军队被勒令撤离该国，结束了法国长达十年的反恐行动，俄罗斯成为该政权的主要外国保护者。
瓦格纳于 2025 年 6 月将其在马里的行动移交给了非洲军团，两年前，普里戈任在莫斯科领导了一场失败的叛变，导致该组织在克里姆林宫眼中名誉扫地。到那年夏天，英国情报机构估计约有 2,000 名非洲军团人员部署在该国。
受到俄罗斯军事情报部门密切监督的非洲军团目前向多个非洲政府提供支持，以换取报酬或获得自然资源的利润丰厚的合同。
尽管有俄罗斯的存在，马里的安全局势仍在继续恶化。 2024 年 7 月下旬，俄罗斯和马里军队在阿尔及利亚边境廷扎瓦滕附近与图阿雷格分裂分子进行了数天的战斗。
瓦格纳当时发表了一份罕见的声明，承认损失，包括一名指挥官的死亡，但没有透露具体数字。俄罗斯消息来源估计死亡人数从 20 人到 80 多人不等。

title_en: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
title_zh: 华为被判窃取商业机密罪，但敲诈勒索罪被判无罪
summary: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
summary_zh: 该判决是在纽约经过长达数月的审判后做出的。
body_en: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.
Huawei said , external the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis", adding that it would "take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests".
Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions.
However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise.
Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada.
Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors.

During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge.
"For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in statement , external .
"Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable."
However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said it was by dint of hard work that Huawei's business had expanded with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff.
Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified that the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

"The RICO [Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act] count that alleged that Huawei was a corrupt organisation, with a corporate culture and policy of committing crime. That was, in our view, a significant overreach, and the jury soundly rejected it," he said.
"Of course, we have mixed emotions about the rest of the verdict ... [we] thought that Huawei was deserving of acquittals across the board."
Sentencing is planned for September 2027. Heberlig said there will be "significant advocacy" to achieve the lowest sentence possible. Following that, he said he fully expects Huawei to appeal.
"If I know Huawei, that fight will continue, and the company's not going to rest until it's pursued every last argument it can through appeal, and hopefully, ultimately toward vindication," he said.
body_zh: 华为被判犯有串谋窃取商业机密和银行欺诈罪，但在美国具有里程碑意义的案件中，华为并没有犯下更严重的总体敲诈勒索罪。
在为期两个月的审判中，检察官指控这家中国科技和电信巨头撒谎、欺骗和盗窃，以获取任何竞争优势。
华为的辩护团队辩称，检察官已经认定华为是一个犯罪组织，并以此为基础立案，但该公司的成功归功于其自身的创新。
华为表示，敲诈勒索案的无罪释放“证实了这些指控缺乏事实依据”，并补充说，它将“采取一切必要的法律行动来捍卫我们的权益”。
布鲁克林一家法院的陪审员裁定华为犯有 12 项罪名中的 10 项，其中包括共谋违反美国制裁。
然而，陪审团拒绝判定华为犯有敲诈勒索共谋罪，该罪名要求陪审团成员发现该公司的行为像犯罪​​企业。
继 2018 年底华为高管孟晚舟在加拿大戏剧性被捕后，联邦检察官于 2019 年首次宣布对华为的指控。
孟晚舟又名孟晚舟，她在加拿大被关押了三年，之后通过与美国检察官的协议获释返回中国。
在上周的结案陈词中，美国助理检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法 (Meredith Arfa) 告诉陪审员，华为花了 20 年时间不择手段地扩大业务，包括就其在伊朗的业务交易向银行撒谎，以及窃取竞争对手公司的技术机密，以确保其拥有竞争优势。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在对外声明中表示：“几十年来，华为及其三个子公司在美国以谎言和盗窃为基础开展业务。”
“感谢联邦调查局和我们联邦检察官的工作，那些参与这些犯罪活动的人将被追究责任。”
然而，辩护律师布赖恩·赫伯利格(Brian Heberlig)表示，通过努力，华为的业务已经扩大，业务遍及170个国家，拥有超过20万名员工。
判决后，赫伯利格告诉 BBC，华为对陪审团驳回敲诈勒索指控感到满意。
“《RICO》（《诈骗影响和腐败组织法》）指控华为是一个腐败组织，具有犯罪的企业文化和政策。我们认为，这是严重的越权行为，陪审团断然拒绝了这一点，”他说。
“当然，我们对判决的其余部分心情复杂……[我们]认为华为应该被全面无罪释放。”
量刑计划于 2027 年 9 月进行。Heberlig 表示，将进行“大力宣传”，以实现尽可能最低的量刑。随后，他表示完全期待华为上诉。
他说：“如果我了解华为，这场斗争将会继续下去，该公司不会停下来，直到通过上诉追寻所有可能的论点，并希望最终得到平反。”

title_en: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
title_zh: 泽连斯基赞扬乌克兰袭击一艘停靠在利比亚海军基地的俄罗斯军舰
summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.
summary_zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，乌克兰对停泊在利比亚港口的一艘俄罗斯军舰进行了袭击，声称海上无人机击沉了该国军舰。
body_en: In this image made from video provided by Russian Defense Ministry Press Service on Sunday, July 16, 2023, a Russian navy corvette Merkury attends naval military exercises in the Baltic Sea. Russian Defense Ministry Press Service/AP hide caption

KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information "if deemed to be appropriate."
The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.
At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.

A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.

Three people were killed Monday in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.

Also on Monday, the European Commission proposed a new round of sanctions to keep economic pressure on Moscow, targeting dozens of Russian banks, cracking down on crypto platforms and slapping bans on sports teams and athletes competing under the country's flag.

The proposals, put forward by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, must be endorsed by all 27 European Union member countries before they can enter into force. The process can take weeks, and the planned measures are likely to be modified.
The bloc has already hit more than 4,700 people and entities, including President Vladimir Putin, and several energy companies.
Zelenskyy lauds Ukrainian attacks from Siberia to Libya
Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.

Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work Monday after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometers (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack.

Russian officials also reported Monday a Ukrainian attack on industrial sites in Russia's Perm region, more than 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from Ukraine. One person was killed in the attack, and 56 Ukrainian drones were downed, Perm Gov. Dmitri Makhonin said.
"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.
body_zh: 在这张根据俄罗斯国防部新闻服务处于 2023 年 7 月 16 日星期日提供的视频制作的图片中，一艘俄罗斯海军护卫舰“水星”号正在波罗的海参加海军军事演习。俄罗斯国防部新闻服务/美联社隐藏标题栏
乌克兰基辅——总统泽连斯基周一表示，乌克兰对停泊在利比亚港口的一艘俄罗斯军舰进行了袭击，并声称海上无人机在前一天的突然袭击中击沉了这艘海军舰艇。
泽连斯基表示，乌克兰军队在地中海袭击俄罗斯海军护卫舰的行动中部署了七架无人机。他在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，这艘名为“水星号”的船只是俄罗斯最新的船只之一，在莫斯科于 2022 年对其邻国发动全面入侵一年后投入使用。
克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫拒绝就此次袭击发表评论，称俄罗斯国防部“如果认为合适”将提供更多信息。
这次行动是在距乌克兰前线约 2,400 公里（1,500 英里）处进行的，是基辅部队最新一次大胆的远程攻击。
战争期间，乌克兰有时会发动袭击，例如 2025 年 6 月的蜘蛛网行动，当时从卡车发射的无人机击中了停在俄罗斯各地空军基地的 40 多架飞机。沿着蜿蜒穿过乌克兰东部和南部的约 1,250 公里（近 800 英里）前线，基辅的无人机和地面机器人正在帮助阻挡俄罗斯规模更大的军队。
与此同时，俄罗斯的导弹和无人机在冬季来临前摧毁了乌克兰的电网，并损坏了民用建筑。
地区警方周一表示，俄罗斯对基辅附近一个村庄的一座五层公寓楼发动袭击，造成 11 人死亡。救援部门称，周日上午的袭击事件后，一名 7 岁儿童和一名 79 岁妇女被从废墟中救出。
地区军事管理局称，俄罗斯周一对乌克兰南部扎波罗热市一家医院发动袭击，造成三人死亡。当局称，俄罗斯军队撞上了一辆带有标记的车辆，表明该车正在从东部城市克拉马托尔斯克疏散居民，造成另外两人死亡。
同样在周一，欧盟委员会提出了新一轮制裁措施，以保持对莫斯科的经济压力，制裁对象是数十家俄罗斯银行，打击加密货币平台，并禁止代表俄罗斯参加比赛的运动队和运动员。
这些提案由欧盟委员会主席乌苏拉·冯德莱恩提出，必须得到所有 27 个欧盟成员国的认可才能生效。该过程可能需要数周时间，并且计划的措施可能会被修改。
该集团已经影响了超过 4,700 名个人和实体，其中包括总统弗拉基米尔·普京 (Vladimir Putin) 和多家能源公司。
泽伦斯基赞扬乌克兰从西伯利亚到利比亚的袭击
泽伦斯基将周日的袭击描述为“典范”，并表示“我们设定的目标已经实现”。
“我们继续在指定水域开展行动。我们正在回应俄罗斯的侵略。我们正在开发乌克兰武器，”他说。
泽伦斯基在柏林举行的北约议会会议上的视频讲话中指出，乌克兰袭击了远至西西伯利亚西部的俄罗斯炼油厂和地中海的俄罗斯军舰。
俄罗斯西部罗斯托夫地区的一家炼油厂周一停止了生产，此前州长尤里·斯柳萨尔表示，乌克兰发动了一场持续了六个多小时的“大规模”无人机和导弹袭击。乌克兰总参谋部表示，该炼油厂距离乌克兰边境仅几十公里，每年可加工多达 5500 万桶石油，在袭击后已起火。
俄罗斯官员周一还报告称，乌克兰对俄罗斯彼尔姆地区的工业场地发动袭击，该地区距乌克兰 1,000 多公里（620 英里）。彼尔姆州州长德米特里·马霍宁 (Dmitri Makhonin) 表示，袭击造成 1 人死亡，56 架乌克兰无人机被击落。
泽伦斯基说：“每次俄罗斯袭击后，我们都在寻找重新站起来的方法。”

title_en: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack
title_zh: 疑似乌克兰无人机袭击后俄罗斯军舰在班加西沉没
summary: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a
summary_zh: 没有人声称对这艘在返回俄罗斯途中停靠的船只的袭击负责 一艘停靠在利比亚港口的俄罗斯军舰
body_en: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.
The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.

Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.

Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

Hours later, a Russia-linked cargo ship said to be carrying military supplies, the Ascalon, was hit by a sea drone off the coast of Benghazi. Video showed the drone heading directly towards one end of the vessel, again causing a huge explosion.

Libyan naval forces ‌rescued the vessel’s crew, the ‌sources added. The health ministry said some crew members were in stable condition with minor injuries. The number of injured and their nationalities are not known.
Benghazi is controlled by the self-styled Libyan National Army, led by Gen Khalifa Haftar, which controls eastern and southern Libya and has been aligned with Russia.

There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range attacks against Russia far beyond the frontlines.
The UN mission in Libya (Unsmil) expressed “serious concern” over the two drone attacks off Benghazi and called for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”, in a post on X.

The ‌eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that ​normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.
It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and ⁠a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take ​legal and ​diplomatic measures against ​anyone found responsible.
“The Libyan government will not ​allow Libyan ‌ports, territory or territorial ​waters ​to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

The specialist website Naval News earlier identified the ship attacked as the Merkury, a Russian corvette – the smallest class of warship, smaller than a frigate – and said it had almost certainly been destroyed.

HI Sutton, a naval analyst, said the attack was probably conducted by sea drones, after a photograph of one emerged apparently taken off the Libyan coast. The drone, he said, “is also likely the type used in the subsequent attack”. Similar-looking drones were involved in the subsequent attack on the Ascalon cargo ship.

If it is confirmed that Ukraine has been able to blow up or seriously damage a Russian warship in Benghazi, it would represent one of its most successful naval strikes during the almost five-year war.
But it also represents a risky extension of the fighting far beyond eastern Europe, in an incident that could affect civilians on another continent and the working of the port.

A small unit of Ukrainian special forces operatives has been based at Misrata, western Libya, and is believed to have coordinated drone attacks on Russian tankers and transport ships in the past year.
body_zh: 没有人声称对这艘在返回俄罗斯途中停靠的船只的袭击负责
周日凌晨，一艘停靠在利比亚港口城市班加西的俄罗斯军舰在疑似乌克兰海上无人机袭击中被击中，导致夜间剧烈爆炸并导致船只沉没。
利比亚东部政府官员表示，这次袭击严重损坏了俄罗斯海军护卫舰“水星”号，该护卫舰当时已停下来加油和补给。
初步报道称，几架乌克兰海上无人机向这艘船发射。官员们告诉美联社，至少四架无人机被拦截并摧毁，其中两架击中了军舰，引发了爆炸。
卫星图像显示，这次袭击发生在距离乌克兰南部1000多英里的地中海，水星号已经沉没，这标志着近五年战争的地理范围显着扩大。
尽管乌克兰在没有海军的情况下开始战争，但它已经发展了海上无人机能力，威胁黑海的俄罗斯军舰。由于被占领的克里米亚塞瓦斯托波尔变得不安全，俄罗斯舰队被迫撤退到新罗西斯克东部港口。
几小时后，一艘据称载有军事物资的与俄罗斯有关的货船阿斯卡隆号在班加西海岸被一架海上无人机击中。视频显示，无人机直接飞向船只的一端，再次引发巨大爆炸。
消息人士补充说，利比亚海军营救了该船的船员。卫生部表示，一些船员受轻伤，情况稳定。受伤人数及其国籍尚不清楚。
班加西由哈利法·哈夫塔尔将军领导的自封的利比亚国民军控制，该军控制着利比亚东部和南部，并与俄罗斯结盟。
俄罗斯当局没有立即做出反应，也没有立即声称对这次袭击负责，但与此同时，乌克兰军队已经加强了对远离前线的俄罗斯的远程攻击。
联合国驻利比亚特派团 (Unsmil) 在 X 上发帖，对班加西附近的两起无人机袭击表示“严重关切”，并呼吁“立即进行独立和透明的调查”。
总部位于东部的利比亚当局表示，包括仓库在内的港口和海军基地设施是安全的，一旦火势得到控制并确保现场安全，就会恢复正常运营。
它谴责这起疑似袭击事件侵犯了利比亚的主权，并对海上安全构成威胁，并表示将对任何责任人采取法律和外交措施。
声明称：“利比亚政府不会允许利比亚港口、领土或领海成为算账或输出国际冲突的竞技场。”
专业网站《海军新闻》早些时候确认，这艘遭到袭击的船只是俄罗斯护卫舰“水星号”——最小级别的军舰，比护卫舰还要小——并表示它几乎肯定已被摧毁。
海军分析家萨顿 (HI Sutton) 表示，这次袭击可能是由海上无人机实施的，因为一张照片显然是在利比亚海岸拍摄的。他说，这架无人机“也可能是随后袭击中使用的类型”。类似的无人机参与了随后对阿斯卡隆货船的袭击。
如果确认乌克兰能够在班加西炸毁或严重损坏一艘俄罗斯军舰，这将是近五年战争中乌克兰最成功的海上打击之一。
但这也代表着战斗有可能延伸到东欧以外的地区，这一事件可能会影响另一个大陆的平民和港口的运作。
乌克兰特种部队的一小支部队驻扎在利比亚西部的米苏拉塔，据信在过去一年里协调无人机袭击了俄罗斯油轮和运输船。

title_en: China-linked network using AI fakes to smear Taiwan election candidates, BBC Verify finds
title_zh: BBC verify 发现与中国有关的网络使用人工智能造假来抹黑台湾选举候选人
summary: The network attacked key figures in the ruling DPP, including President Lai and mayoral candidate Shen.
summary_zh: 该网络攻击了执政的民进党的关键人物，包括赖主席和市长候选人沉。
body_en: Taiwan's ruling party is being repeatedly targeted with AI videos spreading false claims about its leader and other key members ahead of crucial local elections, BBC Verify has found.

A China-linked network has pumped out more than 500 fake videos about the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) in the past year, which experts suggest is part of a long-running campaign to influence the outcome of the elections.

The videos appear to try to smear President Lai Ching-te by claiming he holds a US green card - and would abandon Taiwan if war broke out with China - which Taiwan's presidential office says is completely false. Deepfakes also appear to show Puma Shen, who is running to be the mayor of capital Taipei, using drugs, which he denies. Others seek to undermine or ridicule the politicians by showing them in children's clothing or as popular film characters.

The Taipei mayoralty has traditionally served as a springboard to the presidency. Experts say this has made Shen, who has been openly critical of Beijing, an obvious target for disinformation campaigns. The current mayor, Chiang Wan-an, is part of Taiwan's Kuomintang (KMT) party, which favours closer ties with China.

Taiwan is a self-governing island that China claims as part of its territory. Beijing and Taipei have long observed an uneasy status quo under which Taiwan, backed by the US, neither formally declares independence nor unites with China.

But tensions have risen since the DPP came to power in 2016. Beijing has repeatedly accused the party of pursuing independence while China's leader Xi Jinping, who has said "reunification" with Taiwan is a key goal, has stepped up pressure against the party with increased military activity around the island.
Experts believe the current disinformation activity is part of a broader campaign against Taiwan designed to undermine trust in its democratic process.

"The account operators are trying to make people distrust the DPP politicians so that they will not believe whatever they say," Austin Horng-En Wang, an expert in cognitive warfare at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, told BBC Verify. "If you don't trust that candidate then you will not listen to what they say," he added.

The videos, many of which were shared from an account called "noxparable" or carried a watermark with the same name, have been viewed tens of millions of times across several social media platforms since May 2025.

More than half of those views were tracked in the past four months as the activity has ramped up ahead of the elections. Many of the accounts involved in spreading disinformation listed their locations on social media as mainland China and Hong Kong, while a number of the clips carried labels showing they were generated with AI. Many people who engaged with the videos were often seen repeating the false claims or attacking DPP figures in the comments, while others appeared to treat the clips as entertainment.

One of the most widely shared videos targeted Shen by superimposing his face onto a man who is seen holding a lighter and exhaling smoke alongside claims he is smoking drugs. The video appears to build on accusations from Taiwan's opposition party that he supports drugs decriminalisation, which Shen denies, and was debunked by a local news network.

Shen has taken legal action against people sharing deepfakes, local media reported, while his campaign office said AI videos showing the candidate appeared to be part of a "classic tactic China uses to smear specific targets". BBC Verify contacted the Chinese embassy in London for comment.

Other debunked claims include allegations that Lai's predecessor Tsai Ing-wen had fraudulently obtained her PhD from the London School of Economics. The university pushed back on identical allegations in 2019 and confirmed it had awarded her the doctorate.

A number of the social media accounts BBC Verify identified as sharing the disinformation videos appeared to be linked to Chinese firm Borderless, which produces websites that blend apolitical content with pro-China messaging. The network has also been investigated by journalists at the Taiwanese independent media outlet The Reporter, who shared their findings with BBC Verify. Borderless has previously been accused of carrying out "cognitive warfare" against Taiwan by Taipei's National Security Bureau and the firm has been contacted for comment.

Analysts confirmed to BBC Verify there were also linguistic clues that the accounts, which presented themselves as based in Taiwan, were actually posting from China. The posts occasionally used a simplified Chinese script introduced by the Communist government which was never adopted in Taiwan.

The posts mostly appeared during regular office hours, which Wang suggested showed a "professional" operation, while the accounts originating outside Taiwan showed evidence of election interfering. "When they pretended to be citizens in another country and used these accounts to manipulate the public opinion of the other country during the campaign, it is definitely election interference," Wang added.

Earlier this month, Taiwan's central election commission aired an advert warning voters to "beware of AI-generated deepfake videos" circulating online that could seek to influence the upcoming election. It comes as government officials flagged nearly 2,700 social media accounts to Meta that it claimed were part of a Chinese information warfare campaign, Reuters reported. Meta said it had removed the accounts.

Andrew Yeh of the China Strategic Risk Institute said the ultimate goal is not to favour any party. "China's information operations succeed not just by backing one candidate or opposing another, but by diluting Taiwan's policy debates, driving polarisation and degrading Taiwanese citizens' trust in their democratic processes," he said.
"Regardless of whether the KMT or DPP comes out on top, a more fractured and more divided Taiwan is in Beijing's interests."
body_zh: BBC verify 发现，在关键的地方选举之前，台湾执政党不断成为人工智能视频的目标，传播有关其领导人和其他关键成员的虚假言论。
去年，一个与中国有关的网络发布了 500 多个有关民进党 (DPP) 的虚假视频，专家认为这是影响选举结果的长期运动的一部分。
这些视频似乎试图抹黑台湾总统赖清德，声称他拥有美国绿卡，如果与中国爆发战争，他将放弃台湾，台湾总统府称这完全是错误的。 Deepfakes 似乎还显示，正在竞选首都台北市长的 Puma Shen 使用毒品，但他否认了这一点。其他人则试图通过让政客穿着童装或扮演受欢迎的电影角色来破坏或嘲笑他们。
台北市长职位传统上是成为总统职位的跳板。专家表示，这使得一直公开批评北京的沉成为虚假信息活动的明显目标。现任市长蒋万安属于台湾国民党，主张与中国大陆建立更密切的关系。
台湾是一个自治岛屿，中国声称是其领土的一部分。北京和台北长期以来一直观察到一种令人不安的现状，即台湾在美国的支持下既没有正式宣布独立，也没有与中国统一。
但自民进党2016年上台以来，紧张局势有所加剧。北京方面多次指责该党追求独立，而中国领导人习近平表示，与台湾“统一”是一个关键目标，并通过增加在台湾的军事活动加大了对该党的压力。
专家认为，当前的虚假信息活动是针对台湾的更广泛运动的一部分，旨在破坏对其民主进程的信任。
内华达大学拉斯维加斯分校认知战专家奥斯汀·洪恩·王 (Austin Horng-En Wang) 告诉 BBC verify：“账户运营商试图让人们不信任民进党政客，这样他们就不会相信他们所说的一切。” “如果你不信任那个候选人，那么你就不会听他们说的话，”他补充道。
这些视频大多是从一个名为“noxparable”的账户分享的，或者带有同名水印，自 2025 年 5 月以来，这些视频在多个社交媒体平台上的浏览量已达数千万次。
随着选举前活动的增加，超过一半的观点是在过去四个月内追踪的。许多参与传播虚假信息的账户在社交媒体上将其所在位置列为中国大陆和香港，而一些剪辑则带有标签，显示它们是由人工智能生成的。许多观看这些视频的人经常在评论中重复虚假言论或攻击民进党人物，而其他人似乎将这些视频视为娱乐。
最广泛传播的视频之一是针对沉的，将他的脸叠加到一名拿着打火机、呼出烟雾的男子身上，并声称他正在吸毒。该视频似乎是基于台湾反对党对他支持毒品合法化的指控，沉否认了这一点，并被当地一家新闻网络揭穿。
据当地媒体报道，沉对分享深度伪造品的人采取了法律行动，而他的竞选办公室表示，显示该候选人的人工智能视频似乎是“中国用来抹黑特定目标的经典策略”的一部分。 BBC Verify联系了中国驻伦敦大使馆请其置评。
其他被揭穿的说法包括指控赖智的前任蔡英文以欺诈手段从伦敦经济学院获得博士学位。该大学在 2019 年反驳了同样的指控，并确认已授予她博士学位。
BBC Verify 发现的一些分享虚假信息视频的社交媒体账户似乎与中国公司 Borderless 有关，该公司制作的网站将非政治内容与亲中国信息融合在一起。台湾独立媒体《The Reporter》的记者也对该网络进行了调查，并与 BBC verify 分享了他们的调查结果。无国界此前曾被台北国家安全局指控对台湾进行“认知战”，并已联系该公司置评。
分析师向 BBC verify 证实，还有语言线索表明，这些自称位于台湾的账户实际上是从中国发布的。这些帖子偶尔使用共产党政府引入的简体中文文字，但台湾从未采用这种文字。
这些帖子大多出现在正常办公时间，王认为这显示出“专业”操作，而来自台湾以外的账户则显示出干扰选举的证据。王补充说：“当他们冒充他国公民，并在竞选期间利用这些账户操纵他国舆论时，这绝对是干扰选举。”
本月早些时候，台湾中央选举委员会播放了一则广告，警告选民“谨防网上流传的人工智能生成的深度伪造视频”，这些视频可能会影响即将到来的选举。据路透社报道，政府官员向 Meta 举报了近 2,700 个社交媒体账户，称这些账户是中国信息战活动的一部分。 Meta 表示已删除这些账户。
中国战略风险研究所的安德鲁·叶表示，最终目标是不偏袒任何一方。他说：“中国的信息行动的成功不仅在于支持一位候选人或反对另一位候选人，还在于淡化台湾的政策辩论、推动两极分化并降低台湾公民对其民主进程的信任。”
“无论国民党还是民进党获胜，一个更加分裂和更加分裂的台湾都符合北京的利益。”

title_en: Phone spying to missiles: Why India-Israel strategic ties go beyond Modi
title_zh: 电话间谍导弹：为什么印以战略关系超越莫迪
summary: The opposition Congress party calls Israel’s war on Gaza a genocide, but its leader still wants strong ties with Israel.
summary_zh: 反对派国大党称以色列对加沙的战争是种族灭绝，但其领导人仍然希望与以色列建立牢固的关系。
body_en: Share Phone spying to missiles: Why India-Israel strategic ties go beyond Modi on social media

New Delhi, India – For the past three years, India’s main opposition party, the Indian National Congress, has frequently criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government for its refusal to condemn Israel’s war on Gaza, acknowledging it as a genocide.

Yet when asked about his position on Israel in an interview last week, the party’s de facto leader, Rahul Gandhi, was more nuanced. He condemned Israel’s genocidal war but added: “I support a strong relationship with Israel. We have strategic interests, including buying the best weapons for our armed forces.”

Those comments sparked a backlash from some of the Congress party’s allies, including left parties. But analysts said they reflect the depth of a strategic partnership that, while controversial, is seen as critical by both India and Israel. It’s a relationship that has grown dramatically under Modi but extends beyond his Hindu majoritarian Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government and is one that is likely to outlast its rule.

From weapons and surveillance to policing and hacking, India has increasingly turned to Israel as a vital partner and source of expertise, binding the two countries in ways that are hard to disentangle even if the political winds shift in either nation.

This month, an investigation by the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), a nonprofit, found that Home Minister Amit Shah had waived India’s own rules to allow the purchase of phone-hacking technology from Israel.

Indians have been here before. In 2019, WhatsApp disclosed that Pegasus spyware , developed by Israel’s NSO Group, had been used to target Indian journalists and human rights defenders. Amnesty International later confirmed infections on the phones of journalists Siddharth Varadarajan and Anand Mangnale. The government denied unauthorised surveillance.

Together, the cases point to a dependency, analysts said. India’s cooperation with Israel “has always involved examining and exploring Israeli methods for intelligence gathering, border management and controlling dissent”, researcher and author Azad Essa told Al Jazeera.

“It was only a matter of time before Israeli products or methods would be used against Indians themselves, including farmers,” added Essa, author of Hostile Homelands, a book on the burgeoning alliance between India and Israel.

In Haryana, Delhi’s neighbouring state, the government there spent six years trying to replicate Israeli police and army tactics, and in February 2024, state police used drones to fire tear gas at farmers marching towards Delhi.

The phone tools are the newest layer of a relationship that runs deep into India’s defence industry. Since 2014, India has become Israel’s most reliable arms buyer, taking about 37 percent of its exports.

At the centre of this relationship sits the Adani Group, led by billionaire Gautam Adani, widely seen as a close Modi associate. In 2016, the Indian conglomerate formed a joint venture with Israel’s Elbit Systems to make Hermes 900 drones in Hyderabad, the first such facility outside Israel. Since 2020, Adani has held a 51 percent stake in BLR Systems, which makes Negev machinegun parts with Israel Weapon Industries. In January 2023, Adani and Israel’s Gadot completed the $1.15bn purchase of Haifa’s port, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu attended the handover.
Essa says India “is increasingly becoming a manufacturing and supply base for Israeli companies”.

Ashutosh Singh, an independent researcher in New Delhi who studies Palestine and the Middle East, agreed, calling Hyderabad the best example of Indian capital embedded in Israel’s military infrastructure built “in the garb” of the Make in India initiative, a programme meant to indigenise manufacturing.

Nicolas Blarel, an associate professor of international relations at Leiden University in the Netherlands, added a note of caution. What happens in Hyderabad is “mostly late assembly” of Israeli-designed drones, he told Al Jazeera, and it is “not clear how much technology has been actually completely shared”. But he noted that deliveries were made to Israel in late 2023 and early 2024 when some of those drone models were being used for the genocide in Gaza.

Amnesty International’s “Made in India” report, published on July 30, documented 2,596 shipments of weapons, ammunition and military components from Indian firms to Israel from October 7, 2023, to November 30, 2025, referring to a period that began with the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel that served as the trigger for the assault on Gaza.

It named nine companies, three of them wholly owned by India’s Ministry of Defence, and concluded that the Indian state itself was transferring weapons whenever those firms export. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the next day that India had a “robust” legal framework for strategic trade without addressing the allegations.
Ask analysts why India keeps buying from Israel, and the answer is less about technology than about what Israel does not demand in return.

Kabir Taneja of the Observer Research Foundation think tank said defence carries almost the entire relationship. A country that sells India a Western platform may refuse to share the source code needed to fit an Indian-built missile on it. Israel has been willing to bridge those gaps, for instance by fitting early-warning radars to a Russian Il-76 aircraft.

“Israel is that Walmart of defence technologies that you can just go and purchase without any terms and conditions that stop you from using these technologies in whatever manner is required,” Taneja told Al Jazeera.
body_zh: 手机间谍活动和导弹：为什么印度和以色列的战略关系在社交媒体上超越了莫迪
印度新德里 — — 过去三年来，印度主要反对党印度国大党经常批评总理纳伦德拉·莫迪政府拒绝谴责以色列对加沙的战争，并承认这是一场种族灭绝。
然而，当上周在接受采访时被问及他对以色列的立场时，该党事实上的领导人拉胡尔·甘地的说法更为微妙。他谴责以色列的种族灭绝战争，但补充道：“我支持与以色列建立牢固的关系。我们有战略利益，包括为我们的武装部队购买最好的武器。”
这些言论引发了国大党一些盟友的强烈反对，其中包括左翼政党。但分析人士表示，它们反映了战略伙伴关系的深度，尽管存在争议，但印度和以色列都认为这一战略伙伴关系至关重要。这种关系在莫迪的领导下急剧发展，但超出了印度教多数党印度人民党（BJP）领导的政府范围，而且很可能比其统治更长久。
从武器和监视到治安和黑客攻击，印度越来越多地将以色列视为重要的合作伙伴和专业知识来源，以一种即使两国政治风向发生转变也难以解开的方式将两国联系在一起。
本月，非营利组织互联网自由基金会（IFF）的一项调查发现，内政部长阿米特·沙阿（Amit Shah）放弃了印度自己的规定，允许从以色列购买电话窃听技术。
印度人以前来过这里。 2019年，WhatsApp披露以色列NSO集团开发的Pegasus间谍软件已被用来针对印度记者和人权捍卫者。国际特赦组织后来证实记者 Siddharth Varadarajan 和 Anand Mangnale 的手机受到感染。政府否认未经授权的监视。
分析人士表示，这些案例都表明存在依赖性。研究人员兼作家阿扎德·埃萨告诉半岛电视台，印度与以色列的合作“一直涉及审查和探索以色列情报收集、边境管理和控制异议的方法”。
“以色列的产品或方法迟早会被用来对付印度人本身，包括农民，”《敌对家园》一书的作者埃萨补充道，该书是一本关于印度和以色列之间迅速发展的联盟的书。
在德里邻邦哈里亚纳邦，当地政府花了六年时间试图仿效以色列的警察和军队战术。2024年2月，该邦警方使用无人机向正向德里进发的农民发射催泪瓦斯。
电话工具是深入印度国防工业关系的最新层面。自2014年以来，印度已成为以色列最可靠的武器买家，约占以色列出口的37%。

这种关系的核心是由亿万富翁高塔姆·阿达尼领导的阿达尼集团，他被广泛视为莫迪的亲密伙伴。 2016年，这家印度企业集团与以色列埃尔比特系统公司成立了一家合资企业，在海得拉巴生产Hermes 900无人机，这是以色列以外的第一家此类工厂。自 2020 年以来，阿达尼持有 BLR Systems 51% 的股份，该公司与以色列武​​器工业公司生产内盖夫机枪零件。 2023年1月，阿达尼与以色列加朵完成了11.5亿美元对海法港口的购买，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡出席了交接仪式。
埃萨表示，印度“正日益成为以色列公司的制造和供应基地”。
新德里研究巴勒斯坦和中东的独立研究员阿舒托什·辛格对此表示同意，他称海得拉巴是印度资本融入以色列军事基础设施的最佳例子，该基础设施是“印度制造”计划的“外衣”，该计划旨在实现制造业本土化。
荷兰莱顿大学国际关系副教授尼古拉斯·布拉雷尔(Nicolas Blarel)补充了一条警告。他告诉半岛电视台，海得拉巴发生的情况“大部分是以色列设计的无人机的后期组装”，并且“不清楚有多少技术实际上已经完全共享”。但他指出，这些无人机是在 2023 年底和 2024 年初交付给以色列的，当时其中一些无人机型号正被用于加沙的种族灭绝。
国际特赦组织 7 月 30 日发布的“印度制造”报告记录了 2023 年 10 月 7 日至 2025 年 11 月 30 日期间，印度公司向以色列运送了 2,596 批武器、弹药和军事零部件，该报告指的是从哈马斯领导的对以色列南部的袭击开始的时期，这也是对加沙袭击的导火索。
报告点名了九家公司，其中三家由印度国防部全资拥有，并得出结论称，只要这些公司出口，印度政府本身就在转让武器。印度外交部发言人兰迪尔·贾伊斯瓦尔 (Randhir Jaiswal) 第二天表示，印度拥有“健全”的战略贸易法律框架，但没有回应这些指控。
如果问分析师为什么印度不断从以色列购买产品，答案不是技术问题，而是以色列不要求回报的问题。
观察家研究基金会智囊团的卡比尔·塔内贾表示，国防几乎承担着全部关系。向印度出售西方平台的国家可能会拒绝分享安装印度制造的导弹所需的源代码。以色列一直愿意弥补这些差距，例如在俄罗斯伊尔 76 飞机上安装预警雷达。
塔内贾告诉半岛电视台：“以色列是国防技术的沃尔玛，你可以直接去购买，没有任何条款和条件阻止你以任何需要的方式使用这些技术。”

title_en: The Gambia election: Can the next president deliver on a decade of promise
title_zh: 冈比亚选举：下一任总统能否兑现十年的承诺
summary: Gambians head to the polls amid economic hardship and unfulfilled promises of reform and justice.
summary_zh: 冈比亚人在经济困难和未兑现的改革和正义承诺的情况下前往投票。
body_en: Share The Gambia election: Can the next president deliver on a decade of promise on social media

Banjul, The Gambia – As Gambians prepare to vote on December 5, unemployment, rising living costs, unreliable public services and delayed justice are testing the country’s democratic transition. Nearly a decade after Yahya Jammeh’s departure, voters are asking whether the next president can deliver the change they were promised.
For Sosseh Jagne, the election is about more than who occupies the State House. It is about whether the next government can create conditions in which Gambians can earn a living.

Jagne established Ya Anna’s Catering in 2020 and expanded it into a restaurant in early 2025. But frequent electricity outages have disrupted her business, affecting food preparation, refrigeration and customer service. Between August and October, she said, power cuts sometimes lasted 19 hours or longer.
She estimates that spoiled food cost her more than 40,000 Gambian dalasis ($532). She has also stopped selling homemade iced juices because she cannot guarantee they will remain properly chilled.
“Electricity is not a luxury; it is a necessity for people’s everyday lives and, especially, for businesses that depend on it to operate,” she told Al Jazeera.

Her experience reflects the pressures facing households and businesses as President Adama Barrow seeks a third term. He is one of eight candidates in the December 5 election, according to the Independent Electoral Commission. Barrow came to power in 2017 after defeating Jammeh, who ruled the country for 22 years.
For many young Gambians, the central question is where they can find work.

The 2025 Gambia Labour Force Survey puts overall unemployment at 8.3 percent, up from 7.6 percent in 2022–23. Among people aged 15 to 35, unemployment stands at 11.5 percent. The survey also found that 41.3 percent of young people in that age group were neither employed nor in education or training.

For 26-year-old Maram Mendy, a graduate of the University of The Gambia, finding a job has become increasingly discouraging. Her parents sacrificed to finance her education, making her inability to find work particularly difficult.
“I’m now fed up with looking for a job,” she told Al Jazeera.
She said employers frequently demand previous experience, leaving graduates caught in a cycle: They cannot get a job without experience, but cannot gain experience without employment.
For 28-year-old Buba Sanneh, unemployed since graduating in 2023, the frustration has prompted thoughts of travelling to Europe through irregular migration, commonly known as the backway.

For Hakeem Touray, the search for opportunities abroad has already cost his family dearly. His elder brother, Bob, was 27 when he attempted the journey to Europe in 2021. He died trying to cross the Mediterranean Sea.
Hakeem said the loss highlighted the consequences of unemployment, poverty and limited opportunities at home.

The risks are reflected in figures cited by UN Special Rapporteur Morris Tidball-Binz, following his visit to The Gambia in October 2026. In his end-of-mission statement, he said independent sources had reported that 1,603 Gambians died attempting irregular migration in 2024 and 893 in 2025, most of them at sea. Separately, the International Organization for Migration had recorded at least 408 Gambians missing along migration routes since 2014.
For families, these are not simply statistics but lives lost and loved ones whose fate remains uncertain.

Economic hardship extends beyond unemployment. According to figures published by the Gambia Bureau of Statistics, 53.4 percent of the population – about 1.1 million people – lived below the national poverty line in 2020. The rate was particularly high in rural areas, at about 76 percent, compared with 34 percent in urban areas.
At Bakoteh Market, 38-year-old vegetable seller Fatoumatta Jawara said rising prices have made supporting her family increasingly difficult. She also wants affordable healthcare to become a priority.
“Survival is becoming harder with each passing day. We need a president who will improve our lives for the better,” she told Al Jazeera.
body_zh: 分享 冈比亚选举：下一任总统能否在社交媒体上兑现十年的承诺
冈比亚班珠尔 — — 当冈比亚人准备 12 月 5 日投票时，失业、生活成本上升、公共服务不可靠和司法迟缓正在考验该国的民主转型。叶海亚·贾梅 (Yahya Jammeh) 离职近十年后，选民们开始询问下一任总统是否能够实现他们所承诺的变革。
对于索塞·贾涅 (Sosseh Jagne) 来说，选举不仅仅关乎谁占据州议会大厦。这关系到下届政府能否为冈比亚人创造谋生条件。
Jagne 于 2020 年成立了 Ya Anna's Catering，并于 2025 年初将其扩展为一家餐厅。但频繁的停电扰乱了她的生意，影响了食物准备、冷藏和客户服务。她说，8 月至 10 月期间，停电有时会持续 19 小时或更长时间。
她估计，变质的食物让她损失了超过 40,000 冈比亚达拉西（532 美元）。她还停止销售自制冰果汁，因为她无法保证它们能够保持适当的冷藏状态。
“电力不是奢侈品；它是人们日常生活的必需品，尤其是依赖电力运营的企业，”她告诉半岛电视台。
她的经历反映了总统阿达玛·巴罗寻求第三个任期时家庭和企业面临的压力。据独立选举委员会称，他是 12 月 5 日选举的八名候选人之一。巴罗在击败统治该国 22 年的贾梅后于 2017 年上台。
对于许多年轻的冈比亚人来说，核心问题是他们在哪里可以找到工作。
2025 年冈比亚劳动力调查显示，总体失业率为 8.3%，高于 2022-23 年的 7.6%。 15岁至35岁人群的失业率为11.5%。调查还发现，该年龄段的年轻人中有41.3%既没有工作，也没有接受教育或培训。
对于 26 岁的冈比亚大学毕业生马拉姆·门迪来说，找工作变得越来越令人沮丧。她的父母为资助她的教育做出了牺牲，这使得她找不到工作特别困难。
“我现在厌倦了找工作，”她告诉半岛电视台。
她说，雇主经常要求有经验，这让毕业生陷入了一个循环：没有经验就找不到工作，没有就业就无法获得经验。
28 岁的布巴·桑内 (Buba Sanneh) 自 2023 年毕业以来一直处于失业状态，这种挫败感促使他考虑通过非正常移民（俗称回程）前往欧洲。
对于哈基姆·图雷来说，寻找出国机会已经让他的家人付出了高昂的代价。他的哥哥鲍勃 (Bob) 2021 年尝试前往欧洲时年仅 27 岁。他在穿越地中海的过程中不幸身亡。
哈基姆表示，这次损失突显了失业、贫困和国内机会有限的后果。
联合国特别报告员莫里斯·蒂德博尔-宾兹在 2026 年 10 月访问冈比亚后引用的数据反映了这些风险。他在任务结束声明中表示，独立消息来源报告称，2024 年有 1,603 名冈比亚人在尝试非正常移徙时死亡，2025 年有 893 名冈比亚人死亡，其中大多数死于海上。另外，国际移民组织记录自 2014 年以来至少有 408 名冈比亚人在移民路线上失踪。
对于家庭来说，这些不仅仅是统计数据，而是失去的生命和命运仍不确定的亲人。
经济困难不仅限于失业。根据冈比亚统计局公布的数据，2020年，53.4%的人口（约110万人）生活在国家贫困线以下。农村地区这一比例尤其高，约为76%，而城市地区为34%。
在 Bakoteh 市场，38 岁的蔬菜销售商法图玛塔·贾瓦拉 (Fatoumatta Jawara) 表示，价格上涨让她养家糊口变得越来越困难。她还希望负担得起的医疗保健成为优先事项。
“生存变得越来越困难。我们需要一位能够改善我们生活的总统，”她告诉半岛电视台。

title_en: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
title_zh: 乌克兰申请加入北约和增强防空能力仍存在争议
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
summary_zh: 乌克兰总统泽伦斯基呼吁迅速接纳乌克兰加入北约。然而，为此缺乏必要的一致意见
body_en: It took a while for the video call to connect. When Volodymyr Zelenskyy finally greeted the delegates in Berlin, applause broke out. The Ukrainian president appealed to the gathered parliamentarians from 32 NATO member states to keep supporting his country, especially against the massive aerial bombardment from Russia .

"Dear friends, winter is now ahead of us. And of course, our number one priority is air defense," Zelenskyy told the delegates. His country urgently needs more Patriot and other comprehensive anti-air attack systems. "And your countries have them. Missiles that can stop Russian ballistic missiles should not be sitting in warehouses collecting dust. And we say this openly. Please help us with this."
Western allies boost Ukraine's defenses but clash over deep strikes
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Zelenskyy renewed his call for his country to join the NATO military alliance. That issue is not for the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, which was gathered for its 72nd annual meeting in Berlin, to decide. But it was important to the Ukrainian president to reiterate his request.

After the war ends, Ukraine needs strong security guarantees and NATO could ensure those. "Wouldn't it be more effective to simply bring Ukraine into NATO?" Zelenskyy asked, arguing: "Wouldn't that be better for all of us, for everyone? Cheaper to put in place? And more reliable when it comes to actually protecting security?"

There is conflict among NATO members about the possibility of admitting Ukraine. The alliance has affirmed multiple times that the path to membership stands open to Ukraine — however, in the long term rather than the near future. This is primarily because of the ongoing war and the possible assistance obligations of other NATO countries for Ukraine, which was attacked by Russia.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte rejected the Ukrainian demands at the summit, which for the first time in 26 years was held in Berlin. Ukraine had entry prospects; however, NATO members currently lack unanimity on this issue. NATO alone decides who becomes a member. "There is total clarity on that within the alliance," Rutte said.
If Russia attacked NATO, would Germany be prepared?
Merz: Denying Ukraine NATO membership in 2008 'was a mistake'

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for Ukraine to receive security guarantees similar to what NATO members have, in the instance of a possible ceasefire. In retrospect, it was clear "what a mistake it was not to follow the American suggestion back in 2008 at the NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine as a member," Merz said at a joint press conference following a meeting with Rutte.

Whether or not a NATO entry for Ukraine could be part of negotiations with Russia is another question, according to Rutte. He approved of current US efforts to bring about peace talks, and how Europe was closely consulting with Ukraine and the US for a unified position. "But it is also to test now whether Putin is willing to play ball, and then these issues might come up again."

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to NATO arming itself on a massive scale. Members have committed to raising their countries' defense spending to 5% of their gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.

Rutte warned that all the allies needed a credible path to get there, "and ideally, they get there sooner than 2035." In addition, he said weapons production among member states needed to further increase because "right now, demand still far exceeds the supply."
Why Germany's military ambitions face a battle at home
Germany's military budget has had a massive increase

The contribution by Germany's Bundeswehr armed forces to NATO was explained by Carsten Breuer, Germany's highest-ranking soldier. For example, the massive increase in military spending: "Our defense budget has tripled since 2021. The goal is to achieve the 5% target, which was set at the summit in The Hague, well before 2035." In the coming year, Germany's defense budget has risen to more than €139 billion ($151 billion).

The Bundeswehr was further developing into a "constantly modernized, effective and innovative army, Breuer said. Also, a much larger one than before. "To reach our current capability goals we are expanding the Bundeswehr to a total of 460,000 soldiers by the mid-2030s," the German chief of defense said. Of those, 200,000 are to be reservists. "This is like walking a tightrope because we must find the right balance between growth and operational readiness."
body_zh: 视频通话花了一段时间才接通。当弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基最终在柏林向代表们致意时，爆发出热烈的掌声。乌克兰总统呼吁来自32个北约成员国的议员继续支持乌克兰，特别是反对俄罗斯的大规模空袭。
“亲爱的朋友们，冬天即将来临。当然，我们的首要任务是防空，”泽连斯基告诉代表们。他的国家迫切需要更多的爱国者和其他综合防空系统。 “你们的国家也有它们。能够阻止俄罗斯弹道导弹的导弹不应该被放在仓库里积满灰尘。我们公开这么说。请帮助我们。”
西方盟友加强乌克兰防御，但因深度打击发生冲突
要观看此视频，请启用 JavaScript，并考虑升级到支持 HTML5 视频的网络浏览器
泽连斯基再次呼吁本国加入北约军事联盟。这个问题不应该由在柏林召开第 72 届年会的北约议会来决定。但对乌克兰总统来说，重申他的要求很重要。
战争结束后，乌克兰需要强有力的安全保障，而北约可以确保这些保障。 “直接让乌克兰加入北约不是更有效吗？”泽伦斯基问道：“这对我们所有人、每个人来说不是更好吗？实施起来更便宜？而且在实际保护安全方面更可靠？”
北约成员国之间对于接纳乌克兰的可能性存在冲突。该联盟多次确认，乌克兰的加入之路是开放的——不过，这是从长远来看，而不是在不久的将来。这主要是因为持续的战争以及其他北约国家可能对遭受俄罗斯袭击的乌克兰承担援助义务。
北约秘书长马克·吕特在峰会上拒绝了乌克兰的要求，此次峰会是26年来首次在柏林举行。乌克兰有进入前景；然而，北约成员国目前在这一问题上缺乏一致意见。北约独自决定谁成为其成员。 “联盟内部对此非常清楚，”吕特说。
如果俄罗斯攻击北约，德国会做好准备吗？
梅尔茨：2008年拒绝乌克兰加入北约“是一个错误”
德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨主张，在可能停火的情况下，乌克兰应获得类似于北约成员国的安全保证。默茨在与吕特会面后举行的联合新闻发布会上表示，回想起来，“2008年北约布加勒斯特峰会上没有听从美国的建议，接纳乌克兰为成员国，这是一个多么错误的错误”。
吕特表示，乌克兰加入北约是否可以成为与俄罗斯谈判的一部分是另一个问题。他赞同美国目前为促成和平谈判所做的努力，以及欧洲如何与乌克兰和美国密切协商以达成统一立场。 “但现在也是为了测试普京是否愿意合作，然后这些问题可能会再次出现。”
俄罗斯入侵乌克兰导致北约大规模武装自己。成员国承诺到2035年将各自国家的国防开支提高到国内生产总值(GDP)的5%。
吕特警告说，所有盟友都需要一条可靠的途径才能实现这一目标，“理想情况下，他们能在 2035 年之前实现这一目标。”此外，他表示成员国之间的武器生产需要进一步增加，因为“目前需求仍然远远超过供应”。
为什么德国的军事野心面临国内战斗
德国军事预算大幅增加
德国最高级别士兵卡斯滕·布洛伊尔解释了德国联邦国防军武装部队对北约的贡献。例如，军费大幅增加：“自2021年以来，我们的国防预算增加了两倍。目标是在2035年之前实现海牙峰会制定的5%的目标。”明年，德国的国防预算将增至超过 1,390 亿欧元（1,510 亿美元）。
布洛尔说，德国联邦国防军正在进一步发展成为一支“不断现代化、高效和创新的军队。而且，规模比以前大得多。为了实现我们目前的能力目标，我们将在 2030 年代中期将德国联邦国防军的士兵总数扩大到 46 万人。”德国国防部长表示，其中 20 万人将成为预备役军人。“这就像走钢丝，因为我们必须找到适当的平衡。”在增长和运营准备之间。”

title_en: Kilmar Ábrego García leaving US for Spain, ending Trump deportation battle
title_zh: 基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚离开美国前往西班牙，结束特朗普驱逐战
summary: His deportation to El Salvador and return to the US became a flash point in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.
summary_zh: 他被驱逐到萨尔瓦多并返回美国成为唐纳德·特朗普总统移民议程辩论的焦点。
body_en: Kilmar Ábrego García, whose deportation last year to El Salvador sparked a bitter deportation battle, is leaving the US for Spain.
He is set to take a commercial flight to the country on Tuesday, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

After the government admitted it had wrongfully sent Ábrego García to his home country, he was returned to the US to face human trafficking charges, which were later dropped. The administration then continued its attempts to send him to other countries, including Uganda and Ghana.
His deportation and return became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.
Ábrego García, who is married to a US citizen and lived in Maryland, came to the US illegally from El Salvador as a teenager.
Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland, visited Ábrego García while he was in the notorious Cecot prison in El Salvador in 2025 and advocated for his release.

"A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego García to rot in a Salvadoran gulag," Van Hollen said in a statement on Tuesday. "Today, Kilmar is travelling to a country of his choice, a free man - unharmed and with dignity."
In a statement, Ábrego García's lawyer said his departure was "temporary" as he had "many options to return to the United States".

"We don't expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland," the statement said.
"Where he goes from here, where he chooses to settle for the next two years while he waits out the end of this administration, will be his choice, not the administration's choice."
The BBC has contacted the US Department of Homeland Security for comment.

Ábrego García was arrested in 2019 alongside three other men and detained by federal immigration authorities. A judge granted him protection from deportation to El Salvador at the time, citing the risk of persecution by a gang there.

In March 2025, the Trump administration deported him to El Salvador, where he was held in Cecot, a prison known for its harsh conditions. The US Supreme Court then ordered the government to facilitate his return.

The administration admitted that he was deported in error and brought him back to the US where he was set to face human trafficking charges. A federal judge dismissed the case, saying Ábrego García had been charged for political reasons.
For months, he was locked in a battle over deportation with the government.
Ábrego García had repeatedly said he would be willing to be deported to Costa Rica, and the Costa Rican government had agreed to accept him as a refugee and provide him with legal status.
After reports emerged that the administration was considering sending him to Uganda, a judge barred the government from deporting Ábrego García to a third country.
At one point the Trump administration requested that the judge lift the order so that Ábrego García could be deported to Liberia, CBS reported.
Judge dismisses criminal case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia
body_zh: 基尔马·阿夫雷戈·加西亚 (Kilmar Ábrego García) 去年被驱逐到萨尔瓦多，引发了一场激烈的驱逐战，他即将离开美国前往西班牙。
据英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，他将于周二乘坐商业航班飞往该国。
在政府承认错误地将阿布雷戈·加西亚遣返回国后，他被遣返回美国接受人口贩运指控，但后来被撤销。随后，政府继续尝试将他送往其他国家，包括乌干达和加纳。
他的驱逐和返回成为唐纳德·特朗普总统移民议程辩论的热点。
阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 与一名美国公民结婚，住在马里兰州，十几岁时从萨尔瓦多非法来到美国。
2025 年，马里兰州民主党参议员克里斯·范霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 探访了阿夫雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García)，当时他正在萨尔瓦多臭名昭著的塞科特监狱 (Cecot)，并主张释放他。
范霍伦在周二的一份声明中表示：“一年半前，特朗普政府希望让基尔马·阿布雷戈·加西亚在萨尔瓦多的古拉格集中营里腐烂。” “今天，基尔马正在前往他选择的国家，一个自由人 - 没有受到伤害，并且有尊严。”
阿布雷戈·加西亚的律师在一份声明中表示，他的离开是“暂时的”，因为他“有很多选择返回美国”。
声明称：“我们预计这不会在本届政府领导下发生，我们知道这永远不会给他带来公平的待遇，但我们预计下一届政府将优先考虑让这个家庭团聚并将他带回马里兰州。”
“他从这里走向何方，在等待本届政府结束期间选择在未来两年定居何处，将是他的选择，而不是政府的选择。”
BBC 已联系美国国土安全部征求意见。
阿布雷戈·加西亚 (Ábrego García) 于 2019 年与其他三名男子一起被捕，并被联邦移民当局拘留。当时，一名法官保护他免遭驱逐到萨尔瓦多，理由是他有遭受当地帮派迫害的风险。
2025年3月，特朗普政府将他驱逐到萨尔瓦多，并被关押在以条件恶劣而闻名的塞科特监狱。美国最高法院随后命令政府为他的回国提供便利。
政府承认他被错误地驱逐出境，并将他带回美国，并在那里面临人口贩运指控。一名联邦法官驳回了此案，称阿布雷戈·加西亚因政治原因受到指控。
几个月来，他与政府就驱逐出境问题陷入了争论。
阿夫雷戈·加西亚曾多次表示，他愿意被驱逐到哥斯达黎加，哥斯达黎加政府也同意接受他作为难民，并为他提供合法身份。
有报道称政府正在考虑将他送往乌干达，一名法官禁止政府将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到第三国。
据哥伦比亚广播公司报道，特朗普政府一度要求法官取消该命令，以便将阿布雷戈·加西亚驱逐到利比里亚。

title_en: Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
title_zh: 战后两年，叙利亚地雷伤亡人数激增
summary: Nearly 1,000 children are among those killed or injured by explosives left over from the conflict, figures show.
summary_zh: 数据显示，近 1000 名儿童被冲突遗留爆炸物炸死或炸伤。
body_en: Eleven-year-old Alaa was tending her family's goats with her siblings in a field behind their home in Umm Khuzaym, north-west Syria, on Sunday when there was a flash and a deafening bang.
"Then we heard people screaming," Alaa's father, Walid Mohammed Al-Ghafar, told the BBC.
Walid ran outside to find his daughter lying face down, killed, and her 10-year-old brother, Mahmoud, seriously injured.
Unwittingly, the children had triggered a landmine.

The incident and others this week bring to nearly 1,000 the number of children killed or injured by explosive ordnance in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, according to the UN Mine Action Service (Unmas).
The village is one of many where families have returned to homes and farmland that were once on the front lines of Syria's 13-year civil war.
Alaa's father said demining teams had visited several times to clear the fields. He and other residents believed it was safe for farmers and children to move around.
But mines and other explosives can lie far beyond former battle lines, making it difficult to establish which areas are safe.

"Remnants of war from today's conflicts are often very widely and broadly scattered, often without patterns, which makes it extremely difficult to do clearance," Katrin Atkins, research lead at Landmine Monitor, a global mine monitoring initiative, told the BBC.
The dangers are reflected in a sharp rise in casualties across Syria.

A total of 1,602 people were killed or injured by landmines and explosive remnants of war in 2025 alone, an increase of more than 50% on the previous year, according to the Landmine Monitor report, published by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines on Tuesday.
Only Myanmar, with 1,891 casualties, recorded more.
The report attributes the rise in Syria partly to the large-scale return of refugees and internally displaced people following Assad's overthrow.

"When you look at population movement, a couple of months later you see an increase of incidents in these areas, because that's exactly where people go and start to use the fields again," Atkins said.

More than 60% of casualties recorded by the world's largest landmine clearance charity, the Halo Trust, involve farming, agriculture or shepherding, according to its Syria programme manager, Simon Jackson.
"They're not going to wait for the government or for organisations like us to come and tell them that everything is safe and clear," he told the BBC. "People are taking risks out of desperation."
Since Assad's fall on 8 December 2024, Unmas has recorded at least 1,556 incidents in Syria involving explosive ordnance.
They have caused 2,701 casualties: 935 people killed and 1,766 injured. Children account for 995 of those victims, or about 37%.
But the toll is likely to be higher, with experts estimating that overall casualties could be under-reported by 25-50%.
For many of those who survive, the consequences are devastating and permanent.
body_zh: 周日，11 岁的阿拉和她的兄弟姐妹在叙利亚西北部乌姆胡扎姆家后的田野里放羊，突然一道闪光和一声震耳欲聋的巨响。
“然后我们听到人们尖叫，”阿拉的父亲瓦利德·穆罕默德·加法尔告诉英国广播公司。
瓦利德跑到外面，发现他的女儿脸朝下倒地身亡，而她 10 岁的弟弟马哈茂德受了重伤。
孩子们无意中触发了地雷。
据联合国地雷行动处 (Unmas) 称，自 2024 年 12 月巴沙尔·阿萨德倒台以来，这一事件和本周发生的其他事件导致叙利亚境内因爆炸物造成的儿童死亡或受伤人数接近 1,000 人。
该村是许多家庭返回家园和农田的地方之一，这些地方曾经是叙利亚 13 年内战的前线。
阿拉的父亲说，排雷队已经多次前往清理田地。他和其他居民相信农民和儿童的活动是安全的。
但地雷和其他爆炸物可能远远超出以前的战线，因此很难确定哪些区域是安全的。
全球地雷监测组织地雷监测组织的研究负责人卡特琳·阿特金斯 (Katrin Atkins) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，“当今冲突中的战争遗留物往往非常广泛且分散，而且往往没有模式，这使得清理工作变得极其困难。”
这些危险体现在叙利亚各地伤亡人数急剧上升。
国际禁止地雷运动周二发布的地雷监测报告显示，仅 2025 年，就有 1,602 人因地雷和战争遗留爆炸物丧生或受伤，比上一年增加了 50% 以上。
只有缅甸的伤亡人数最多，有 1,891 人。
报告将叙利亚局势的崛起部分归因于阿萨德被推翻后难民和国内流离失所者的大规模回返。
阿特金斯说：“当你观察人口流动时，几个月后，你会发现这些地区的事件有所增加，因为这正是人们去的地方并开始再次使用田地。”
世界上最大的地雷清除慈善机构 Halo Trust 的叙利亚项目经理西蒙·杰克逊 (Simon Jackson) 表示，其记录的伤亡人数中有 60% 以上涉及农耕、农业或牧羊业。
“他们不会等待政府或像我们这样的组织来告诉他们一切都是安全和明确的，”他告诉英国广播公司。 “人们出于绝望而冒险。”
自 2024 年 12 月 8 日阿萨德倒台以来，Unmas 记录了叙利亚至少 1,556 起涉及爆炸物的事件。
已造成 2,701 人伤亡：935 人死亡、1,766 人受伤。其中 995 名受害者是儿童，约占 37%。
但伤亡人数可能会更高，专家估计总伤亡人数可能少报了 25-50%。
对于许多幸存者来说，其后果是毁灭性的、永久性的。

title_en: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
title_zh: 哥伦比亚总统抵达旅游城市超市人质围困现场
summary: Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of an operation involving scores of security personnel trying to free at least 20 hostages Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20
summary_zh: 哥伦比亚总统阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉 (Abelardo de la Espriella) 将负责一项涉及数十名安全人员的行动，试图解救至少 20 名人质
body_en: Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of an operation involving scores of security personnel trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of a operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.
About 30 people were initially seized by the armed men early on Tuesday morning, but by nightfall, 10 hostages – five of them elderly women – had been released, police said.
There have been no reports of injuries so far.

Before arriving in Cartagena, the right-wing president said that, despite the context of growing violence perpetrated by criminal groups involved in the country’s decades-long armed conflict, the hostage-taking appeared to have stemmed from a botched robbery carried out by “common criminals”.
The past few days have been particularly challenging in the South American country, with a car bomb and a drone attack killing one person and leaving nearly 30 injured.

The supermarket where the hostages are being held is just six miles from the old city and its 500-year-old fortress walls overlooking the Caribbean. Hundreds of thousands of visitors are drawn to Cartagena every year.

The gunmen reportedly arrived at about 8.30am local time at an Éxito supermarket in La Castellana neighbourhood and, according to Colombia’s president, the group planned to rob an armoured cash-in-transit vehicle that was due to collect the previous day’s takings from the store.
After spotting the movement on security cameras, employees reportedly alerted the national police, who surrounded the supermarket.

“My son is there,” Jacob Perez, the father of one of the workers reportedly held hostage, told Agence France-Presse. “He didn’t leave work and he’s not answering his phone. I think they took it from him,” he said.
Customers were also believed to be among the hostages. The five people initially released were “older women”, according to De la Espriella.

Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of the supermarket, while local media outlets showed snipers positioned on nearby buildings in what appeared to be a standoff between the armed men and police.
Map showing location of Cartagena in Colombia.

De la Espriella, known for his populist rhetoric and an “iron fist” approach to crime – he sometimes wears a gun on his waist and has posed beside the bodies of people killed by police – has been in office for just over three months, and said the hours-long standoff at the supermarket “will turn out well for the hostages, but I’m not so sure it will turn out quite so well for the hostage-takers”.

He addressed the case at a press conference in Villavicencio, about 684 miles inland, where he was dealing with the aftermath of an attack on Monday night in which a car bomb was detonated outside the headquarters of the Meta departmental government.
More than 20 people were injured and a security guard was killed, and the president attributed the attack to a dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc).

“Narco-terrorism is desperate because we are confronting it decisively. It intends to intimidate us and force us to retreat in search of another false peace process,” the president said, referring to the landmark 2016 peace deal between the government and the Farc – whose signing marked its 10th anniversary on Tuesday.

Internationally recognised for substantially reducing violence, the deal alone could not bring the decades-long armed conflict to a definitive end. Subsequent administrations were slow to implement the agreement, which was rejected by Farc dissidents and other rebel factions.
body_zh: 阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉 (Abelardo de la Espriella) 将接管一项涉及数十名安全人员的行动，试图解救至少 20 名人质
哥伦比亚总统已抵达热门旅游城市卡塔赫纳一家超市内，安全部门与持枪歹徒之间长达数小时的对峙现场，至少有 20 人被扣为人质。
据法新社报道，阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉的车队于周二晚上抵达卡塔赫纳，表面上他将在那里指挥一项涉及数十名军官、海军和特种部队的行动。
警方称，周二清晨，武装人员最初劫持了约 30 人，但到傍晚时分，10 名人质（其中 5 名老年妇女）被释放。
到目前为止，还没有受伤的报告。
在抵达卡塔赫纳之前，这位右翼总统表示，尽管参与该国长达数十年的武装冲突的犯罪团伙的暴力行为日益增多，但劫持人质事件似乎源于“普通罪犯”实施的拙劣抢劫。
过去几天在这个南美国家尤其具有挑战性，汽车炸弹和无人机袭击造成一人死亡、近 30 人受伤。
关押人质的超市距离老城区及其俯瞰加勒比海、拥有 500 年历史的堡垒城墙仅六英里。每年都有数十万游客被吸引到卡塔赫纳。
据报道，枪手于当地时间上午 8.30 左右抵达拉卡斯特拉纳 (La Castellana) 附近的一家 Éxito 超市，据哥伦比亚总统称，该团伙计划抢劫一辆装甲运钞车，该运钞车原本要从商店收取前一天的收入。
据报道，在安全摄像头发现这一动静后，员工向国家警察报警，后者包围了超市。
“我的儿子就在那里，”据报道被劫持的一名工人的父亲雅各布·佩雷斯 (Jacob Perez) 告诉法新社。 “他没有下班，也没有接电话。我认为他们把电话从他手中拿走了，”他说。
据信，人质中还包括顾客。德拉埃斯普里埃拉表示，最初释放的五人是“老年妇女”。
社交媒体上分享的视频显示，数十人冲出超市，而当地媒体则显示，附近建筑物上部署了狙击手，武装人员与警察之间似乎发生了对峙。
显示卡塔赫纳在哥伦比亚的位置的地图。
德拉埃斯普里埃拉以其民粹主义言论和打击犯罪的“铁拳”手段而闻名——他有时腰上挂着枪，并在被警察杀害的人的尸体旁摆姿势——上任仅三个多月，他表示超市长达数小时的对峙“对人质来说会有好结果，但我不太确定对人质劫持者来说会有那么好结果”。
他在距离内陆约 684 英里的比亚维森西奥举行的新闻发布会上谈到了这一事件，当时他正在处理周一晚上发生的袭击事件的后果，当时一枚汽车炸弹在梅塔省政府总部外引爆。
造成 20 多人受伤，一名保安人员死亡，总统将此次袭击归咎于哥伦比亚革命武装力量 (Farc) 的一个持不同政见派系。
“毒品恐怖主义是绝望的，因为我们正在果断地对抗它。它意图恐吓我们，迫使我们撤退，以寻求另一个虚假的和平进程，”总统说，他指的是2016年政府与哥伦比亚革命武装力量之间具有里程碑意义的和平协议——周二该协议的签署标志着该协议签署十周年。
该协议因大幅减少暴力而得到国际社会的认可，但仅靠该协议并不能彻底结束长达数十年的武装冲突。随后的政府在执行该协议方面进展缓慢，并遭到哥伦比亚革命武装力量持不同政见者和其他叛乱派别的拒绝。
